items.evidence: repository.githubId/fullName/name/stars/forks/language/pushedAt/license/state are all mapped in the research note’s Page field evidence table to F1/F2; editorial.summary, editorial.audience, editorial.features, and editorial.stack are likewise mapped to F3–F6.
editorial.hook, editorial.meaning, editorial.opportunity, and all three directions are marked inferred in the research note, each with basis facts F3–F6 and separate Direction rationale entries.
程序已逐项核对 githubId、fullName、许可证、仓库状态、fetchedAt、Star、Fork 与 pushedAt；项目值与本轮 GitHub 原始快照完全一致，计数保持整数且未转成实时描述。

No contradictions found between project JSON and research note: repository.state=active matches F1; license is the same AGPL-3.0/ GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 metadata family; unfetched/live values are avoided by the snapshot note stating stars/forks/push are captured facts, not live values.
editorial.hook is a concrete project trait phrase (“把文件处理搬进内网工厂”) grounded in F3/F4, not a generic praise claim.
editorial.summary states inputs (图片、视频、音频、PDF 和通用文件), core actions (UI、REST API、pipelines; 转换、压缩、OCR、转写、去元数据、local AI), and visible result (处理结果留在你自己的网络中).
editorial.summary plus editorial.features cover more than three verified capabilities: multi-type file handling (F4), image editor / OCR / transcribe / local AI / pipelines / REST API (F5).
The summary keeps usable product terms like UI, REST API, pipelines, OCR, local AI, and self-hosted; it does not over-explain low-level implementation details.
hook and summary are separated: hook is a short memory phrase, while summary carries the full product picture and does not repeat the hook sentence verbatim.
editorial.summary describes only SnapOtter’s current behavior; editorial.meaning stays at reuse value (“适合从一整套大平台里拆出更小、更明确的产品”) and does not present new features as existing ones.

editorial.meaning gives overall reuse value, and each editorial.opportunity item links validated capabilities (OCR / pipelines / REST API) to a concrete new product possibility and friction reduction.

project.editorial.audience names original users; each direction has its own audience, approach, and scope, with approach describing the workflow and scope listing only the minimal supporting functions.
archive-tray has a specific user group (财务、行政、法务和档案人员) and recurring problem (扫描件和 PDF 手工整理很慢), with input/output steps named in its approach.
archive-tray’s approach names inputs (扫描件、图片和 PDF), core steps (OCR、拆分、合并、脱敏、加页码或签名), and output (导出归档包).
archive-tray explicitly reuses OCR, PDF tools, UI, REST API, and self-hosted storage from F3/F4/F5/F6; its workflow/user/output differ from the base project by narrowing to document archiving only.
archive-tray.scope has 5 items and is closed to the stated workflow: 上传、OCR、拆分/合并/脱敏、签名/页码、导出归档结果.
archive-tray, media-pipeline, and internal-file-api differ on at least two of user/input/workflow/result (e.g., archive vs media vs API); they are not just rename-only variants.
Each direction states a concrete benefit: archive reduces manual整理, media reduces碎片化工具操作, and API removes the need to stitch external SaaS together.
At least one direction is non-commercial/creative by default: media-pipeline serves content creation and personal素材整理 rather than marketing/sales/赚钱 flows.
